title: Base composition explains the slower evolution of the 3′UTR-derived part of 2,290 human processed pseudogenes; primate divergence excludes extra 3′UTR constraint above about 2%
abstract: The 3′UTR-derived part of human processed pseudogenes has fewer variants and substitutions than the coding-derived part. Its lower mutation rate explains this difference. This matters because a 2018 study used it as the main genome-wide evidence that pseudogenes are microRNA sponges (competing endogenous RNAs, ceRNAs) under selection. A processed pseudogene is a DNA copy of a messenger RNA that was inserted back into the genome. We mapped 6,792 autosomal processed pseudogenes to their parent mRNAs. We analysed the 2,290 with at least 50 usable sites in each part. The coding-derived part has more GC (46.8% vs 39.6%) and 1.9 times as many CpG sites, which mutate fast. We re-tested the 2018 statistic on its 20-species alignment (1,881 pseudogenes, anthropoid primates). Raw divergence was 5.9% lower in the 3′UTR part (ratio 0.941; Wilcoxon P = 6e-36). We then removed sites that were CpG in the parent mRNA and compared with a composition-matched expectation from flanking DNA. The ratio became 0.998 (95% interval 0.985-1.012; Wilcoxon P = 0.31), and it stayed between 0.998 and 1.006 under all alignment filters in primates. Substitutions on the human lineage and variants in 76,215 genomes (gnomAD v4.1) agreed (corrected ratios 0.999-1.017). The same methods detect selection in the parent mRNAs: their coding sequence has 21% fewer variants and 69% fewer substitutions than expected. Expressed pseudogenes (GTEx TPM 1 or more) showed no detectable 3′UTR constraint. At microRNA sites inherited from the parent, pseudogenes had no variant deficit (ratio 1.000, 0.979-1.021), whereas parent sites had 5.0%. Assumptions and limits: flanking DNA is neutral; gnomAD cannot detect constraint on whole 3′UTRs; weak selection at intact microRNA sites is not excluded. Short-read filters exclude young pseudogenes that are nearly identical to their parents, such as PTENP1, and two chromosomes are missing from the 20-species test. Thus, genome-wide conservation does not support pseudogene ceRNA function. We did not test single pseudogenes.

display.caption: Re-test of the 2018 evidence on its own alignment (UCSC 20-way; 1,881 pseudogenes, anthropoid primates, strict parent-alignment filter). Ratio of the 3prime-UTR-derived to the CDS-derived part: raw (open) and against a composition-matched expectation (filled), with all sites and with parent-CpG sites removed; human-lineage (orange) and gnomAD (green) readouts with CpG-prone sites removed. Lines: 95% bootstrap intervals; Wilcoxon P: per-pseudogene test of the 2018 design.

Ratio of the 3prime-UTR-derived to the CDS-derived part of 2,290 human processed pseudogenes (left) and of their parent mRNAs (right; positive control), before (open) and after (filled) a neutral mutation model, for gnomAD variants and human-lineage substitutions. The parent mRNAs show strong coding constraint; the pseudogenes do not differ between parts after the model.

Why the raw difference occurs: the CDS-derived part is GC-richer and has 1.9 times as many CpG sites as the 3prime-UTR-derived part and flanking DNA (left). Raw share of possible variants seen in gnomAD (middle) and observed/expected after the mutation model (right), by mutation type.
